texts.preamble: State vs Sanjay Bansal on 12 July, 2025 State Vs. Sanjay Bansal In The Court Of Ms. Payal Singal Judicial Magistrate First Class-09, Central, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi State vs. Sanjay Bansal Fir No. : 16/2017 U/S : 285/338 Ipc Ps : L. Gate Cr. Case No. : 13543/2017 Judgment
texts.facts: It is the case of the prosecution that at that time, in order to save PAYAL SINGAL SINGAL 2025.07.12 18:06:46 +0530 State Vs. Sanjay Bansal himself, the injured jumped from 3rd floor and sustained grievous injuries as the accused did not place any order or adequate equipment or extinguisher to prevent fire and thus the accused knowingly and negligently omitted to take such order with the fire or combustible matter in the possession of accused above-said purpose as is sufficient to take guard against any probable danger to human life and personal safety of other from above said fire on the 2nd and 3rd floor of said property and thereby the accused committed an offence punishable under Section 285/338 IPC. 2) After completion of the investigation, the chargesheet was filed in the court, upon which cognizance was taken and after complying with the provisions of Section 207 Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as Cr.P.C.), arguments on the point of charge were heard and the formal charge was framed u/s 285/338 Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as IPC) against State vs Sanjay Bansal on 12 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185391682/ 1 the accused person on 06.03.2020 to which the accused person pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Thereafter, the case was proceeded further for prosecution evidence. PROSECUTION EVIDENCE 3) Before proceeding with the prosecution evidence, it is relevant to mention here that during the course of trial, the accused person had admitted the copy of FIR No. 16/2017 (Ex. AD1); endorsement made on rukka (Ex. AD2); Certificate U/s 65 B Indian Evidence Act (Ex. AD3), DD FIR No. 16/2017, PS L. Gate Page No. 2 of 14 Digitally signed by PAYAL PAYAL SINGAL SINGAL Date: 2025.07.12 18:06:59 +0530 State Vs. Sanjay Bansal No. 8 A dated 03.02.2017 (Ex. AD4), Fire report no. 201879125 dated 05.03.2017 (E.X. AD5), MLC No. EEB001870 alongwith medical report dated 03.02.2017 (Ex. AD6) and X-Ray report CR. No. 001870 (Ex. AD-7) without admitting the contents of the said documents. Thus, the said witnesses were not summoned. 4) Accordingly, to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined the remaining 03 witnesses in support of its case i.e. PW-1 Sh. Ram Sewak, PW-2 ASI Bhimesh and PW-3 Retired SI Pratap Singh. Now, the testimonies of all these witnesses shall be discussed in detail one by one. 5) PW-1 Ram Sewak deposed that on 03.02.2017, he was present at IIIrd Floor of Paneer Bhandar (Kharkhana), Khari Baoli owned by Sh. Sanjay Bansal as on 02.02.2017, he came in Delhi on shop of accused Sanjay for seeking work of Helper for preparing and Sweets and Namkeen as his fellow villagers were also working at aforesaid shop/kharkhana. PW-1 deposed that on 02.02.2017, in the night, he slept at IIIrd Floor at the aforesaid shop/kharkhana and his fellow villager namely Bade @ Ramhet, told him that there is no work with his employer accused Sanjay at that time and therefore he will arrange some work for him within 2-4 days at any other place. Then, PW-1 deposed that as he was about to leave the said shop/kharkhana at around 8 AM, he heard noises coming from below floor of the said shop a fire is breakout due to leakage of gas from the cylinder at shop/kharkhana. PW- 1 FIR No. 16/2017, PS L. Gate Page No. 3 of 14 by PAYAL PAYAL SINGAL Date: SINGAL 2025.07.12 18:07:08 +0530 State Vs. Sanjay Bansal then stated that he was at the third floor at that time and as he was coming down from the third floor by stairs, there was fire coming upside from Stairs/Jeena, then he again coming up towards third floor in order to save himself from the fire flames which were raising towards third floor and on reaching the third floor, he went towards Tin Shade in order to take shelter, however, the fire flames and smoke reached there. PW-1 further deposed that he came out of the said Shed in nervousness and fear and that then, he came in contact with fire flames and got burn injuries in his left hand and arm and State vs Sanjay Bansal on 12 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185391682/ 2 his shirt was also burnt. Then, in order to save himself from further burning of the said fire, he jumped on the roof of the adjunct building which was below one level than the building in which fire broke out and during this process, his left leg/foot was also got fractured when he jumped from the building. The witness further stated that the fire broke-out as there was no order, equipment or fire extinguisher installed by the accused/owner Sanjay in the said shop in order to prevent the fire accident of such nature and that the fire broke-out due to the rash and negligence of the owner/accused Sanjay. Thereafter, PW-1 stated that he was taken to the LNJP Hospital by Ambulance where he received his treatment and th police took his statement in the hospital Ex. PW-1/A. PW-1 further deposed that he had told about the place of incident to police in his complaint and on the basis of which the site plan was prepared by IO. The said witness correctly identified the accused and the Digitally FIR No. 16/2017, PS L. Gate Page No. 4 of 14 signed by PAYAL PAYAL SINGAL SINGAL Date: 2025.07.12 18:07:16 +0530 State Vs. Sanjay Bansal photographs of the spot of the crime. 6) PW-2 ASI Bhimesh deposed that on 03.02.2017, he was posted as HC as PS Lahori Gate and on the said date, at about 8:00 am, a PCR call was marked to ASI Pratap Singh and after receiving the same, he along with ASI Pratap reached at Property no. 169, Haryana Mishthan, Gali Abdul Hakeen Tilak Bazar, where the fire was broken-out on the 2nd and 3rd floor. PW-2 stated that they got to know that the injured namely Ram Sevak S/o Gulab Singh was taken to Hospital LNJP and ASI Pratap Singh instructed him to remain at the spot and ASI Pratap himself went to the LNJP Hospital. Then, PW-2 deposed that after some time, ASI Pratap Singh returned to the spot and handed over tehrir to him for the registration of the FIR whereafter, he left the spot and went to the PS Lahori Gate, where he handed over the Tehrir to the concerned DO for the registration of the FIR. After registration of the same, PW-2 stated that he returned to the spot where he handed over the computerized copy of the FIR along with the original Tehrir to ASI Pratap. PW-2 then deposed that IO served the notice to the owner of the building and got to know that the fire was broke out due to the short circuit. The said witness correctly identified the accused and the photographs of the spot of the incident. 7) PW-3 Retired SI Pratap Singh deposed that on 03.02.2017, he was posted as ASI at PS Lahori Gate and on the said date at about 8:30 am, DD no. 8A was marked to him and after receiving the same, he along with HC Bhimesh FIR No. 16/2017, PS L. Gate Page No. 5 of 14 Digitally signed by PAYAL PAYAL SINGAL SINGAL Date: 2025.07.12 18:07:24 +0530 State Vs. Sanjay Bansal reached at the spot ie property no.169 Haryana Sweet Bhandar, Hakeem Wali Gali, Tilak Bazar, where fire was broke out on the 2nd and 3rd floor on the above said premises. The witness deposed that State vs Sanjay Bansal on 12 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185391682/ 3 the fire-brigade was already there and tried to stop the fire and on inquiry, he got to know that the injured namely Ram Sevak was already removed from the spot by the CAT Ambulance to the LNJP Hospital. Then, PW-3 deposed that he left HC Bhimesh at the spot and went to LNJP Hospital, where he met with the injured Ram Sevak and received his MLC and also recorded his statement Ex.PW1/A. Thereafter, PW3 stated that he returned to the spot where he prepared tehrir Ex.PW3/A and handed over the same to the HC Bhimesh for the registration of the FIR who left the spot and went to PS Lahori Gate. After some time, PW-3 stated that HC Bhimesh returned to the spot and handed over the computerized copy along with the original tehrir to him. Thereafter, PW-3 deposed that he prepared site plan Ex. PW3/B; he also clicked the photographs of the spot through his mobile phone and the same was placed on record Ex. P1 to P10; he also received the opinion pertinent to the nature of the injury caused to the victim Ram Sevak and it opined by the concerned Doctor as in grievous in nature. PW-3 then stated that he also served notice U/s 41A Cr. PC to the accused on 05.12.2017 Ex.PW3/C and on the next day, the accused Pankaj Bansal reached at the PS and joined the investigation. Thereafter, after completion of all the formalities, the witness stated to Digitally FIR No. 16/2017, PS L. Gate Page No. 6 of 14 signed by PAYAL PAYAL SINGAL SINGAL Date: 2025.07.12 18:07:33 +0530 State Vs. Sanjay Bansal have prepared the challan and filing the same in court. 8) All the witness were duly cross examined by the Ld. Defence counsel wherein some material facts have come on record which shall be duly dealt with in the reasoning part of the judgment. STATEMENT OF THE ACCUSED: 9) After recording the testimony of all the witnesses, the PE was closed and thereafter, the statement of the accused Sanjay Bansal was recorded u/s 313 Cr.P.C. r/w S.281 Cr.P.C on 22.05.2025. In the said statement, the accused person denied all the allegations levelled against him and stated that he had been falsely implicated in the present case. The accused person further stated that he did not want to lead any DE and accordingly, the matter came up for final arguments.
texts.arguments: FINAL ARGUMENTS: 10) Arguments on behalf of the accused person were advanced by ld. counsel Sh. Prabhat Ranjan and by Sh. Rohit Lohat, Ld. APP on behalf of the State. 11) It was argued by Ld. APP for the state that the state had successfully proved its case beyond all reasonable doubts that it was due to the rashness and negligence of the accused person, who being the owner of the premises i.e. property no. 169, Abdul State vs Sanjay Bansal on 12 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185391682/ 4 Hakim wali, Tilak Bazar, Delhi FIR No. 16/2017, PS L. Gate Page No. 7 of 14 Digitally signed by PAYAL PAYAL SINGAL SINGAL Date: 2025.07.12 18:07:41 +0530 State Vs. Sanjay Bansal failed to take proper care and precaution qua the said property that fire broke out in the same which caused grievous injuries to the inhabitant of the building namely RAM Sevak. It was argued that the testimony of the injured stood the test of cross-examination and no material contradictions could be brought in the same and accordingly, when the same is corroborated with the testimony of police witnesses leaves no iota of doubt regarding the guilt of the accused. Accordingly, it was has argued that the accused be convicted for offences u/s 285/338 IPC. 12) Per contra, it was argued by the Ld. counsel for the accused person that the accused person was completely innocent and had been falsely implicated in the case. It was further argued that as per the testimony of PW-1, he was never an employee of the accused neither did he work in the shop of the accused in which scenario, it cannot be said that he suffered injuries in any fire that may have broken out at the shop of the accused. It was then argued that no investigation was done by the police officials qua the security apparatus installed in the shop including the fire extinguisher and even upon the cause of the fire, if any and accordingly, it cannot be said that the fire broke out due to any rashness or negligence on behalf of the accused. Lastly, it was argued that no other workers or public persons were examined by the prosecution to establish the presence of the injured at the spot. Accordingly, it was argued that the alleged recovery was planted on the Digitally signed by PAYAL PAYAL SINGAL Date: SINGAL 2025.07.12 18:07:55 +0530 State Vs. Sanjay Bansal accused person and it was prayed that the accused person be acquitted of all charges levelled against him. 13) Arguments from both the sides have been heard and the record has been carefully perused. REASONS FOR THE JUDGMENT Negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter.--Whoever does, with fire or any combustible matter, any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any fire or any combustible matter in his possession as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from such fire or combustible matter, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both". "338. Causing grievous hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others.--Whoever causes grievous hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or FIR No. 16/2017, PS L. Gate Page No. 9 of 14 Digitally signed by PAYAL PAYAL SINGAL SINGAL Date: 2025.07.12 18:08:07 +0530 State Vs. Sanjay Bansal negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both." 16)
